resources.string: A quiet breathing aid for winding down before sleep.
This is a relaxation aid, not medical treatment for insomnia.
Stop immediately if you feel dizziness, shortness of breath, pain, panic, or discomfort.
Works offline. No account or network connection is needed.
Choose a session length, start while the screen is visible, then turn the display off and follow the gentle cues.
Keep the phone uncovered and in a comfortable position. Do not place it under a pillow or body weight.
Choose a preset or slide to a custom breathing session length.
Choose inhale and exhale separately from 2 to 10 seconds in half-second steps. The default is 6 seconds for each phase.
Slide from 0 to 20 minutes. Choose at least 1 minute to start.
0 minutes selected. Move the slider above zero to start.

Notifications are off, so turn the display back on if you need to use the in-app stop control.

This app uses slow-paced breathing with a six-second inhale and a six-second exhale by default. Adjust each phase in whole or half seconds with the timing sliders. Hold time is zero seconds. Keep the breath natural and comfortable rather than forcing its depth.

By default, breathe in gently for 6 seconds, breathe out gently for 6 seconds, then repeat. Use the timing sliders to choose each phase in whole or half seconds. There is no breath hold between phases.

Research links slow breathing below 10 breaths per minute with relaxation-related changes. A small pre-sleep study used about 6 breaths per minute for 20 minutes. Broader evidence is promising but inconclusive, so this is not presented as the fastest or guaranteed way to fall asleep.
A gentle vibration marks the beginning of each phase. Breathe in during the inhale phase and out during the exhale phase. The cues help with timing and do not require a particular breath depth.
1. Choose a session length, then adjust inhale and exhale timing in whole or half seconds.
2. Start while the screen is visible and keep the phone uncovered in a comfortable position.
3. Turn the screen off and follow the inhale and exhale cues.
4. Stop whenever you need to, or let the session finish naturally.
For persistent insomnia, cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia has stronger evidence than a breathing timer. Sleep Inducer is a wellness aid, not a treatment.
